Article Title: Delhi HC seeks Centre's response on body cameras on cops during protests
Article Text:
Delhi HC asks Centre to consider mandatory body cameras for police

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has asked the Centre to consider a PIL seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras by police during protests and crowd-control operations, saying the issue should not be treated as a “grey area” requiring court intervention.The court asked the Centre to take a decision on the plea within six months.A bench headed by Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambhre said any direction on the use of body-worn cameras would have wider implications for policing and could not be confined to the Delhi Police alone.The bench observed while hearing the plea, “Why should we direct them to legislate? It cannot be said that it is a grey area.”The court questioned the need for judicial intervention when existing laws already provide for regulation of police procedures in areas covered by the legislature.The PIL, filed by Chahat Raghav, seeks directions for the mandatory use of body-worn cameras by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed during protests and crowd-control operations. It also seeks a comprehensive framework governing the storage, retention, integrity and evidentiary use of footage recorded by the cameras.The petitioner has cited the use of body-worn cameras by traffic police and a tender issued for their procurement, arguing that the technology is already available to the authorities.Senior Advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that body-worn cameras could enhance transparency and accountability during protests, especially in cases involving allegations of police excesses and counter-allegations against protesters.Sibal said the cameras were already being used by police in some situations, but only sporadically. He argued that the Delhi Police's 2022 standing order on rallies and demonstrations did not specifically provide for body-worn cameras and that a clear protocol was needed.He also disputed that the existing videography mechanism was sufficient, saying the recording under the standing order was different from footage captured by cameras worn directly by police personnel involved in crowd control.Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the respondents, submitted that the Delhi High Court's PIL rules require a petitioner to first approach the concerned authorities through a representation. He said the present petition could be treated as such a representation.Sharma also submitted that the Supreme Court, while hearing a matter concerning protests at Jantar Mantar, had directed the authorities to frame an SOP and that the existing mechanism already provides for videography of protests. The court recorded the ASG's statement and directed the respondents to communicate their decision on framing an SOP for the use of body-worn cameras within six months.The petitioner was given liberty to approach the High Court again in case of any inaction.The move comes amid heightened security in the New Delhi, Central Delhi and North Delhi districts following a series of demonstrations against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in large numbers, with multilayered barricades placed at several points to prevent protesters from entering restricted areas.
Article Summary: Delhi hc asks centre to consider mandatory body cameras for police during protests. Pil seeks directions for the mandatory use of body-worn cameras by delhi police. Move comes amid heightened security in the new delhi, central delhi and north delhi districts.

Article Title: Who is Vivek Bhagat?: What is the controversy around the Delhi Police officer
Article Text:
File photo: ACP Vivek Bhagat

Who is Vivek Bhagat?

What are the allegations against him?

Why is his promotion controversial?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police officer ACP Vivek Bhagat, currently posted as sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) in Connaught Place, has come under scrutiny after three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The complaints were transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial” enquiry. Bhagat has since consented to keeping his current duty charge as additional deputy commissioner of police on hold pending the enquiry.Bhagat is a Delhi Police officer currently serving as SDPO, Connaught Place. He was among 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers assigned the current duty charge of Additional DCP in an order approved by Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu.The Delhi government later modified the order after Bhagat formally requested that the charge concerning him be kept on hold, citing the pending Crime Branch enquiry.Bhagat had also been involved in police action during protests in June, when he was injured amid clashes between protesters and police.During those protests Bhagat said that he was allegedly surrounded and overpowered during the clashes and was beaten, kicked and punched.He reported alleged head injuries, bruises and broken teeth.An ANI report from the time said Bhagat was injured by stone and bottle pelting near Tolstoy Marg. The injuries were sustained while police were dealing with protesters during the June clashes.Three women journalists complained of sexual harassment following a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3.One journalist specifically alleged that Bhagat sexually assaulted her while she was covering the protest. She said she had approached him after noticing that no women police personnel were present while protesters were being detained.According to her complaint, she asked Bhagat about the absence of women personnel, following which he allegedly sexually assaulted and pushed her.The allegations have not been established. The Delhi Police transferred the complaints to its Crime Branch, which is examining the allegations and recording statements of the complainants and other people concerned.The allegations emerged just days before Bhagat was among 12 officers assigned the current duty charge of Additional DCP.A senior police officer said the promotions were routine and that the request for the promotions had been sent much earlier.After the allegations and the pending enquiry came to light, Bhagat wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner saying he consented to keeping the order concerning him on hold until the enquiry was dealt with.The Delhi government subsequently modified the administrative order, putting his Additional DCP charge on hold.The Crime Branch enquiry will determine the facts surrounding the allegations. The complaints remain allegations at this stage, and the material available does not establish that Bhagat committed sexual harassment.The Press Council of India has meanwhile expressed “shock and dismay” over the allegations and urged Delhi Police to act on the journalists’ complaints, saying journalists must be able to work without facing aggression or threats.
Article Summary: Vivek bhagat is a delhi police officer currently serving as sdpo, connaught place. Three women journalists complained of sexual harassment following a protest against chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar at jantar mantar on october 3. The delhi police transferred the complaints to its crime branch, which is examining the allegations and recording statements.

NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on the BJP over law and order in West Bengal, claiming that more than 2,400 rape cases were recorded in the state in just five months.In a post on X, the All India Trinamool Congress cited figures attributed to the State Crime Records Bureau and claimed that 2,454 rape cases were registered during the five-month period.The party also cited figures for other crimes, claiming that Bengal recorded 600 murder cases, 13,114 attempted murder cases and 32,341 cases of assault causing grievous hurt during the same period.“2,400+ RAPE CASES IN BENGAL IN JUST 5 MONTHS UNDER BJP!” the TMC said in its post, accusing the BJP of turning Bengal into a place where women and ordinary citizens are increasingly being forced to live in fear.The party questioned the BJP's claim of ensuring a “safe and secure Bengal”, asking whether the crime figures reflected the reality behind its promises.“Is this the ‘safe and secure Bengal’ BJP promised?” the TMC asked, referring to the BJP's “Bhorsha In, Bhoy Out” slogan.The party said the people of Bengal deserved “security, accountability and justice” rather than what it called “jumlas”.The TMC also directly targeted CM Suvendu Adhikari, accusing him of hiding behind “slogans and hollow promises” and alleging that he had failed the people of Bengal.“YOU have failed the people of Bengal,” the party said, adding that it had been raising the issue since the beginning and that the alleged failures of the BJP were becoming harder to hide.

Article Title: Anant Ambani unites over 50 animal welfare groups under Vantara's ‘Champions of Care’ initiative
Article Text:
"Every day, there are countless people who quietly care for animals in need, often with limited resources and little recognition, but with immense compassion,"

"Their work reminds us that kindness has no boundaries and that every life deserves care, protection and dignity. Through Champions of Care, we hope to stand alongside this work, strengthen the care available to community animals and help build a more compassionate India.

For us, this is what Every Life Matters truly means."

"I deeply appreciate Shri Anant Ambani Ji’s vision and leadership in bringing Champions of Care to life,"

"I have travelled across the world, but have rarely seen an animal care centre where such advanced facilities and technology have been made available for animals, with a level of care comparable to what we aspire to provide for people.

What touched me most was his personal effort to listen to the organisations, understand their challenges on the ground and respond with practical and sustainable solutions. By bringing these organisations together, he is not only recognising their dedication but also strengthening their collective ability to care for animals.

This is a meaningful step towards a more compassionate future for community animals across India."

A national framework for grassroots animal care

Sustainable infrastructure and nationwide collaboration

On World Animal Day, Anant Ambani, Executive Director at Reliance Industries Limited, announced 'Champions of Care', a new national initiative designed to strengthen community animal welfare through practical, sustainable solutions.Convened at Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat, the landmark gathering brought together more than 50 animal welfare organisations from across India, alongside key statutory advisory members, establishing a collaborative framework to elevate animal care standards nationwide.The initiative addresses the critical needs of community animals, including street dogs, cats, abandoned livestock, and working animals such as horses and donkeys. Through targeted support in veterinary care, rescue operations, shelter facilities, and responsible population management programmes, the nationwide network is estimated to reach and support around two million animals every year.At the heart of the movement is the simple recognition that every community animal deserves care, protection, and dignity. Speaking on the launch of the initiative, Anant Ambani highlighted the unsung dedication of grassroots caregivers who work tirelessly across the country.Anant Ambani said.Eight members of the Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) participated in the event. S. P. Gupta, former Chairman and current member of the AWBI, commended the vision and leadership behind the nationwide drive.Gupta noted.The two-day gathering in Jamnagar provided participating delegates with an immersive experience of advanced animal care standards. Representatives toured Vantara's specialised facilities for rescued elephants and big cats, as well as naturalistic environments housing free-roaming species such as bison, zebras, and antelopes. The experience demonstrated how excellence in veterinary medicine, nutrition, housing, and lifelong care can be applied to elevate community animal welfare.Beyond facility tours, the gathering focused on connection, dialogue, and collaborative problem-solving among non-governmental organisations. A key milestone was the signing of a Letter of Understanding between Vantara and all participating organisations, formalising a shared commitment to strengthen community animal welfare. The understanding establishes a framework for knowledge sharing, capacity building, and practical support shaped by ground-level needs.Towards the close of the gathering, each participating organisation was presented with a Certificate of Appreciation signed by Anant Ambani, acknowledging their tireless devotion to animal protection.Rather than relying on short-term assistance, the initiative focuses on long-term organisational capacity and resilience. Vantara will support diverse needs identified by partner groups, including mobile veterinary services, ambulances, rescue tools, and diagnostic and treatment equipment.To help shelters become more self-sustaining and efficient, support will cover sustainable infrastructure upgrades such as solar power systems, rainwater harvesting, and improved drainage systems. Partner organisations also plan to roll out education programmes for youth, alongside quarantine and disease management infrastructure to combat infectious diseases.Conceived as an extension of Vantara's commitment to Every Life Matters, Champions of Care will continue expanding its network in the coming years, creating a connected, unified response to animal welfare across India.
Article Summary: Champions of care is a national initiative to strengthen community animal welfare through practical, sustainable solutions. The initiative addresses the critical needs of community animals, including street dogs, cats, abandoned livestock, and working animals such as horses and donkeys.

Article Title: 'Like your movie, money is Ata Pata Laapata': SC directs Rajpal to pay Rs 2 crore by Oct 13
Article Text:
'Money is Ata Pata Laapata': SC directs Rajpal to pay Rs 2 crore by Oct 13

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore towards the amount due to the complainant in a cheque-bounce case by October 13, saying it would consider his plea against the High Court order after the payment is made.Yadav, who was present in court, brought a demand draft of Rs 1.15 crore, while the remaining Rs 85 lakh is to be paid by October 13 through a buyer of his property, who was also present in court.The court, however, came down heavily on Yadav's conduct and warned that it could enhance his sentence, saying repeated extensions were being granted only to ensure that the complainant received the money.The Court said the deposit was directed to secure the amount due to the complainant and observed that Yadav’s conduct had not satisfied it.“Law should not be utilised like this”, the Court said.After passing the order, the bench had an informal exchange with Yadav, who spoke about the financial difficulties caused by his film Ata Pata Laapata. He said the film had resulted in losses of around Rs 200-250 crore and that the producers had also suffered losses.During the hearing, the Court also remarked in jest that the film's title was synonymous with Yadav's conduct.“Like your movie, your money is also Ata Pata Laapata, gayab”, the CJI said.Before the order was passed, film actor Rajpal Yadav appeared before the Supreme Court for the hearing of a cheque-bounce case against him and said, "The matter is before the honourable Supreme Court, and our legal team and lawyers will speak on the issue. I have the utmost respect for my country and for the Supreme Court. Whatever decision is taken by the court, wherever and whenever it is delivered, will be universally accepted. "Yadav later greeted the bench, saying, “Pranam karta hoon,” and spoke about the losses of Rs 200-250 crore he had incurred over the film.The CJI advised him to make a good film and entertain people, adding in jest that advocates appearing before the Supreme Court were also good actors and could be cast in his films.Yadav's counsel told the Court that he had approached the Registry to make the payment, but RTGS was not permissible. He said the actor had therefore brought a demand draft of Rs 1.15 crore.On the remaining Rs 85 lakh, the counsel said a buyer of Yadav's property was present in court and the amount would be paid once the transaction was completed.Yadav submitted that the dispute arose from a Rs 5 crore liability connected with the film Ata Pata Laapata, while the film had caused much larger losses.The case arises from an alleged loan extended to Yadav by Murli Projects Pvt Ltd in 2010 for Ata Pata Laapata. Seven repayment cheques of Rs 1.05 crore each were subsequently dishonoured.
Article Summary: 'money is ata pata laapata': sc directs rajpal to pay rs 2 crore by oct 13. Yadav brought a demand draft of rs 1.15 crore, while the remaining rs 85 lakh is to be paid by october 13 through a buyer of his property.

Article Title: KPSC recruitment case: Suspended chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, member BV Geetha detained
Article Text:
KPSC Case: ED Arrests Suspended Chairman Sahukar, Member Geetha

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Tuesday detained suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukar and KPSC member BV Geetha after conducting searches at Sahukar's residence in Dollars Colony, Sanjaynagar.Last week, the ED completed questioning suspended IAS officer and former KPSC controller of examinations Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar after taking him into custody. Another accused in the case, self-styled political activist Basavaraj Kannale, was also questioned by the agency. Both Gangwar and Kannale are currently in judicial custody at Bengaluru Central Prison after their bail pleas were rejected by the courts.On Tuesday morning, a team of ED officials reached Sahukar's residence and recorded his statement. He was detained later in the evening. Another ED team picked up KPSC member BV Geetha from her flat in an apartment in Dollars Colony, Sanjaynagar, for questioning.The ED had earlier recorded statements from several candidates, including Suguresh, a close relative of Sahukar who had secured unusually high marks, according to the FIR.Sources said Sahukar was detained based on Suguresh's confession.The investigation has also found that Sahukar allegedly called Gangwar twice on the night of January 7, a day before the examination. Gangwar is accused of sharing the question paper and an answer script with Suguresh, who allegedly later shared them with Geetha.Sahukar, a native of Hemanala village in Raichur district's Devadurga taluk, holds a degree in Agricultural Engineering. He was appointed as a KPSC member in September 2019 and was elevated as chairman in April 2021 by then governor Vajubhai Vala on the recommendation of the state government, succeeding Shadakshari Swamy.Sahukar has also faced scrutiny in a separate case involving allegations that his daughter submitted a fraudulent income certificate showing an annual family income of Rs 40,000 to claim reservation under Category 3B for government employment.The Karnataka High Court had criticised the declaration as a "fraud" and an "eyewash", observing that Sahukar was drawing a substantial salary as KPSC chairman. He was subsequently suspended from office following cabinet recommendations.He is also under investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) over alleged irregularities, paper leaks and cash-for-jobs cases linked to recruitment examinations, including the recruitment of 400 veterinary officers and other gazetted posts.The investigations have alleged the involvement of middlemen and illegal transactions in exchange for candidate selections. His anticipatory bail plea was earlier rejected by the High Court after the CID presented evidence allegedly linking him and his associates to middlemen.The ED is investigating the money-laundering aspects of the alleged recruitment scams and has conducted searches as part of its probe into the financial trail and suspected illicit assets.
Article Summary: Kpsc chairman shivashankarappa s sahukar and kpsc member bv geetha detained. Ed conducted searches atsahukar's residence in dollars colony, sanjaynagar. Last week, ed completed questioning suspended ias officer gyanendra kumar gangwar after taking him into custody.

Article Title: CBI raids CM Bhagwant Mann’s camp office, his OSD’s home in graft probe
Article Text:
Central forces stand guard as CBI searches Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann's camp office in Chandigarh

After CBI raid in graft probe, Punjab CM claims BJP has started poll preparation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH: CBI registered an FIR against Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s OSD Rajbir Ghuman and five others Tuesday, following it up with raids on eight locations, including the CM’s camp office in Chandigarh.The coordinated search came within hours of the state govt moving Supreme Court against Punjab and Haryana high court’s order for a CBI probe into ED’s allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through the OSD.The search at Mann’s camp office in House No 50 of Sector 2 started around 6pm, sending shockwaves through the administration. It was at this office that Ghuman used to allegedly meet the co-accused, said CBI sources. A CBI team also visited Ghuman’s home in his village, Gharachon in Sangrur.CBI said the case was registered following a court order that was based on an ED report. The investigation centres on allegations of corruption and abuse of power and political influence. Apart from Ghuman, those named by CBI in the FIR are Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, RS Nagra and “unknown public servant(s) and private person(s)”.Nitin is alleged to be a “liaison” in the “cash-for-transfer” scandal with access to Ghuman. His brother Jitin was allegedly provided access to CMO through Ghuman and Dr Romi Mahajan, described as an “associate” who allegedly worked with Ghuman and helped coordinate appointments. Devinder is an AAP youth activist and Nagra is a “private associate”.CBI searched premises linked to the accused in Chandigarh, Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar and seized laptops, mobile phones and financial documents.The seized laptops, mobile phones and documents are currently undergoing forensic scrutiny to establish evidence of bribery, official impropriety, and financial paper trails.Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann responded through a post on X in Punjabi, “BJP has started preparations for Punjab elections. A CBI raid was conducted at my camp office. Now ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab so that Punjab govt and I can be defamed. BJP is in panic as it sees the love received from people.”CBI said the FIR is meant to investigate allegations of corruption against OSD to CM, Rajbir Ghuman, and his associates for “influencing and manipulating postings of officers, including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land-related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits”.“It is also alleged that the accused public servants purportedly accessed and provided drafts of orders and policies to private persons prior to their issuance by the govt,” said CBI, adding that those named in the FIR include two public servants, middlemen, and associates.ED had conducted searches in Punjab from May 7-10 in a PMLA case and written to the DGP on July 30 to register a case.Advocate Nikhil Saraf filed a PIL in HC, alleging ED had written three letters to the Punjab DGP, seeking registration of an FIR against Ghuman and others, yet Punjab Police didn’t do so.On Monday, a division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor heard the PIL and said, “We are not impressed by the manner in which Punjab Police has acted so far and, therefore, deem it appropriate to entrust investigation to CBI.”
Article Summary: Cbi searches premises linked to the accused in chandigarh, mohali, gurdaspur, ludhiana, patiala, sangrur and jalandhar. The seized laptops, mobile phones and documents are currently undergoing forensic scrutiny to establish evidence of bribery.

Article Title: 'Expert in theatrics': BJP hits out at Rahul Gandhi over protest 'drama', row over meeting EC
Article Text:
BJP hits Rahul Gandhi over EC meeting demand, calls protest ‘drama’

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Tuesday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of staging 'drama' over his demand to meet the Election Commission . BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi called the Leader of Opposition 'an expert in theatrics' and alleged that the poll panel’s statement had exposed what he described as Rahul's 'lies'.The remarks came as the confrontation between the Opposition and the Election Commission escalated on Tuesday, with Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra among around 250 people detained during an INDIA bloc protest in Delhi. The leaders were demanding a meeting with chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and his resignation.Addressing a press conference in the national capital, Trivedi said, “All day long, he kept telling the nation that he was being denied a meeting. The Election Commission has clearly stated that no request for a meeting was received from either the INDI Alliance or the Congress party ,” he said.Trivedi said the Commission had an established procedure for such requests and was prepared to meet a delegation of representatives.“Secondly, the Commission noted in its press release that it was only at 4 pm that the police DCP informed them of the Leader of the Opposition's desire to meet,” he said.“However, he insisted on a different approach, claiming that 300 MPs were with him and intending to enter the premises with that entire group, which has never happened in the history of India.There isn’t even enough space there for so many people to sit,” Trivedi said.He further claimed that the Commission had offered an alternative by suggesting that a senior official could visit the protest site to receive a memorandum.“It was suggested that a senior Commission official could visit the protest site to receive the memorandum, but Rahul Gandhi refused that option as well,” he said.“It is evident that he had no real intention of actually presenting his case to the Election Commission,” Trivedi alleged.The Election Commission, meanwhile, said no political party had formally requested a meeting with it by 4 pm. It later said Delhi Police informed it that a delegation led by Rahul Gandhi wished to meet the Commission to submit a memorandum.The poll panel said the proposed meeting involving a large group of MPs at Parliament House Annexe was “unusual and unacceptable”, as established protocol requires such meetings to take place at the Election Commission’s premises. It said it had offered to send its most senior executive officer to receive the memorandum, but the proposal was rejected by the MPs.
Article Summary: Bjp hits rahul gandhi over ec meeting demand, calls protest ‘drama’ bjp mp sudhanshu trivedi called the leader of opposition 'an expert in theatrics' and alleged that the poll panel’s statement had exposed what he described as rahul's 'lies'

Article Title: 'Unusual request': EC explains why it could not meet Rahul Gandhi-led opposition MPs
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi being detained by police personnel after over eight-hour sit-in inside Akashvani Bhawan premises along with several other MPs.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid the onging row with opposition parties over SIR, the Election Commission of India on Tuesday said that no political party had formally sought an appointment to meet."Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission," said the EC in a statement.The EC added that it found out through Delhi Police that "a delegation of MPs, led by the Hon'ble leader of the opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi , wished to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum."Further clarifying the rules and justifying itself, the EC cited procedures laid down for meetings with political parties. "All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly Authorised Representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides," it said.The EC further claimed that after 4 PM, while it was considering the proposed meeting, the Delhi Police informed it that the delegation comprised 240 MPs and that they wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe.The Commission termed the request “unusual” and said it could not be accepted because, under ECI protocol, meetings with political parties are held only at the Commission’s premises.The poll panel said it then offered to send its senior-most officer on duty to the Parliament House Annexe to receive the MPs’ memorandum. The EC described this as “an unprecedented step”, but said the offer was also declined by the MPs.The Commission said it respected “the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country”, while stressing that its own protocols and conventions were also important. It reiterated that political parties can request meetings with the EC at any time, after which the Commission schedules a date and time depending on its availability.This came as INDIA bloc leaders staged a massive march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the poll panel over their allegations of “vote chori” and seeking the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined the sit-in near Akashvani Bhavan, but police later cleared the protest site and detained several opposition MPs.Read more: Rahul and Priyanka removed from protest site after high drama - watch
Article Summary: The election commission of india said that no political party had formally sought an appointment to meet. This came as india bloc leaders staged a massive march from parliament towards the election commission headquarters. Rahul gandhi and priyanka gandhi vadra joined the sit-in near akashvani bhavan, but police later cleared the protest site.

NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded in the heart of Delhi on Tuesday as INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.The day-long protest ended after Delhi Police detained Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, KC Venugopal, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Charanjit Singh Channi, and several other opposition MPs at Akashvani Bhavan, where they staged a sit-in after being denied a meeting with election officials.The protest was part of the INDIA bloc's wider campaign against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Opposition parties have accused the poll panel of disenfranchising eligible voters and have demanded Kumar's resignation. They have also sought the scrapping of the ongoing SIR exercise and the restoration of names they allege were wrongly deleted from electoral rolls.Rahul Gandhi, along with several opposition leaders, began the march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, raising slogans of "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod" and carrying placards and cutouts of Gyanesh Kumar.The protest route saw heavy security deployment, with barricades placed across central Delhi and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed around Transport Bhawan ahead of the march. Police stopped the opposition MPs near the NITI Aayog office.Rahul climbed atop heavy iron barricades near the NITI Aayog office and waved the Tricolour as he attempted to advance towards the EC headquarters.Tensions escalated as Delhi Police detained Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal and several other INDIA bloc leaders near the NITI Aayog office.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Trinamool Congress leaders Abhishek Banerjee, Derek O'Brien and Mahua Moitra, and CPM MP John Brittas were among those put into police buses.The protest took an unexpected turn when Rahul and Priyanka walked into the nearby Akashvani Bhavan, shifting the protest away from the heavily secured route.As police began detaining INDIA bloc MPs and putting them into buses, Rahul spoke to his sister, who was seated inside one of the buses, before making his way towards the reception entrance of Akashvani Bhavan, catching several opposition MPs, including some from his own party, by surprise.At the entrance near gate number 3, Akashvani Bhavan staff initially tried to prevent Rahul Gandhi from entering, leading to a tense stand-off. He eventually entered the premises accompanied by his security personnel.Around 12.45 pm, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal and Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera reached the gate and sought entry. New Delhi deputy commissioner of police Sachin Sharma also arrived and held talks with the leaders, who were subsequently allowed inside.After Rahul and other Congress leaders positioned themselves inside Akashvani Bhavan, mats were laid out and the sit-in began.While Rahul remained mostly seated, Priyanka Gandhi held talks with police officials.Refreshments were brought in for the protesters. Packets of potato chips, bhujiya and chocolates, along with water bottles and soft drinks, arrived from a kiosk outside NITI Aayog. Diet Coke was brought from Patel Chowk, while rolls arrived from Khan Chacha.Later, Srinivas was seen clearing used packets from the area where the leaders had gathered. Mosquito repellent was also brought inside in the evening.The crowd outside Akashvani Bhavan grew as Congress workers gathered and raised slogans in support of Rahul Gandhi.Around 2.30 pm, reporters pushed their microphones through the grille as Rahul spoke to them from inside the premises."I don't care what the BJP says. I am standing here to protect democracy," he said."What has been done to the country is treason. Be it PM Modi, Shah, the RSS chief or Gyanesh Kumar, none will be spared," Gandhi alleged.Amid the protest, the BJP held three press conferences and accused Congress and its allies of creating "anarchy" to "relaunch Rahul Gandhi".The BJP also accused Gandhi of being "kaamchor", alleging that he should work on the ground instead of accusing others of being "vote chor".Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan accused the INDIA bloc of "venting its frustration" over electoral defeats by making baseless allegations against constitutional bodies and attempting to malign their image.BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi criticised the opposition for what he called "theatrics on the streets" and questioned the Congress over its demand to provide voting rights without verification to those identified as "absent, shifted, dead and duplicate" voters.After several hours of protest, Delhi Police cleared the site and detained Rahul and Priyanka along with several opposition MPs, including Pawan Khera, KC Venugopal, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Derek O'Brien and Mahua Moitra.According to Delhi Police, around 260 individuals, including 10 Parliamentarirans, were detained and taken to various police stations in Delhi, where necessary legal action is being taken in their regard. The detainees were taken to New Police Lines at Kingsway Camp.Congress hit out at the Modi government, saying the action was a sign of a regime that "knows its exit is imminent"."Method of disenfranchising Indians has just become murder of democracy in India," Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said."The leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been dragged away from a peaceful sit-in protest that had a simple and straightforward demand - a meeting with the Election Commission of India," Ramesh said in a post on X."The Delhi Police that is controlled by the co-conspirator of the murder of democracy in India has arrested the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and others. This is the sign of a regime that knows its exit is imminent," he added.Meanwhile, the Election Commission said no political party had formally sought an appointment for a meeting with it."Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission," the EC said in a statement.The poll panel said it subsequently learnt through Delhi Police that a delegation of MPs, led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, wanted to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum.The EC said its established procedure requires political parties or joint delegations to seek appointments through their authorised representatives. Meetings are then held at a mutually agreed time at the Commission's premises.The poll panel said that after 4 pm, while it was considering the proposed meeting, Delhi Police informed it that the delegation comprised 240 MPs and wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe.The Commission termed the request "unusual" and said it could not be accepted because, under ECI protocol, meetings with political parties are held only at the Commission's premises.The INDIA bloc's protest was part of its wider campaign against the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. Opposition parties have accused the poll panel of disenfranchising eligible voters and have demanded Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.The bloc has also sought the scrapping of the current SIR exercise and restoration of names it alleges were wrongly deleted from electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi, priyanka gandhi vadra, kc venugopal, amrinder singh raja warring, charanjit singh channi, and several other opposition mps staged a sit-in after being denied a meeting with election officials. The protest was part of the india bloc's wider campaign against the election commission over the special intensive revision (sir) exercise.

Article Title: 'Dhappa': Cops tried to stop INDIA bloc's march to EC; Rahul Gandhi pulled a surprise
Article Text:
How Rahul Gandhi changed the script with a surprise move after INDIA bloc march to EC was stopped

INDIA bloc protest in Delhi

Rahul Gandhi being taken away by cops during July 21 protest.

Rahul Gandhi scales barricades as cops tried to stop protesters.

NEW DELHI: The protest route was planned, and the police were prepared. But then came a “Rahul twist” in the planned script.The INDIA bloc's protest march on Tuesday was supposed to begin at Parliament House and end at the Election Commission headquarters, where opposition MPs planned to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.As expected, central Delhi was heavily barricaded. Police and paramilitary personnel were deployed along the route, traffic diversions were put in place and access to the Election Commission office was restricted.But midway through the protest, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and his sister, Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, pulled a surprise on the cops.As police started detaining INDIA bloc MPs and moving them into buses after stopping the march, Rahul and Priyanka did not remain on the road waiting to be taken away.Priyanka first boarded a bus parked near the building and Rahul prepared to follow her.But then suddenly they changed their course and walked into the nearby Akashvani Bhawan premises, taking their protest away from the heavily secured route to a new location and catching the cops off guard.The two later sat under a tree near Gate No. 4 as staff of the broadcasting house rushed outside to watch the unfolding drama.Outside, the Congress leaders began gathering at the reception entrance, seeking to join the Gandhi siblings inside.Some of them KC Venugopal, Pawan Khera, Imran Pratapgarhi and Srinivas BV subsequently joined the sit-in protest, while others climbed the boundary wall and raised slogans.Later, Congress did not miss the opportunity to flaunt the surprise “detour” and shared a video of the move with a playful 'dhappa' caption. The video showed the protesters changing route just when police appeared to have brought the march under control.This is not the first time Rahul Gandhi has pulled a surprise on the cops during a protest.On July 21, a day after police action against students and youth during a protest at Jantar Mantar against NEET paper leak, Rahul and a group of Congress MPs unexpectedly reached near Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence and began an impromptu sit-in. The move was a surprise not just for the cops but also many Congress leaders who were only told that they were gathering to wish birthday wishes to party chief Mallikarjun Kharge. That protest ended only after police physically removed Rahul and other leaders from outside the PM’s house.This time, Rahul changed his method. He announced a protest plan and started on the planned course. But instead of waiting for police to arrest him, he and Priyanka quickly moved the demonstration to another location.Earlier in the day, Rahul climbed a police barricade and waved the national flag as INDIA bloc MPs attempted to move towards Nirvachan Sadan. Police eventually stopped the march, detained several leaders and began taking them away in buses.Congress leader Pawan Khera hit out at the security deployment that prevented opposition MPs from reaching the poll body to submit their memorandum. Rahul, too, questioned why opposition leaders were being prevented from meeting Election Commissioners."More than 300 opposition MPs marched from Parliament to the Election Commission today to meet the Election Commissioners. We represent crores of Indians. Why aren't the Election Commissioners meeting us? Why is the police stopping and threatening us?" Rahul said.The march was part of the INDIA bloc's wider campaign against the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. Opposition parties have accused the poll body of disenfranchising eligible voters and have demanded Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The INDIA bloc has also sought the scrapping of the current SIR exercise and restoration of names it alleges were wrongly deleted from electoral rolls.The Election Commission has rejected the allegations."The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour. All actions of ECI have been in accordance of laws and instructions of the Commission," the EC had said in an official statement."Differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution. They are a part of the decision-making process before a final decision is taken. Not only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorized to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system," it said.The BJP, meanwhile, accused the opposition of attempting to undermine a constitutional institution. Party spokesperson Sambit Patra alleged that the Congress and its allies were trying to create "anarchy" and use the confrontation with the Election Commission to politically relaunch Rahul Gandhi."A sponsored attempt is being made by opposition parties, especially the Congress, as to how a change of power can be brought about in the country and Rahul Gandhi be made to sit in power just like that. For this, a blow to India's democracy and constitutional bodies is being hurled in a sponsored manner," Patra said.After nearly 9 hours of sit-in, the police forcibly removed Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka and other Congress leaders thus ending the stand-off. This is exactly how Rahul was removed from the protest site in July when he had staged his first impromptu protest.

Article Title: SIR row: Will annul Election Commission orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
‘Decisions must be unanimous or by majority’, says Supreme Court

CEC, ECs need to either rebut or endorse allegations about ‘unilateral decisions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday asked the Election Commission , CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to clarify whether crucial decisions regarding the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls were taken unilaterally by the CEC, and said it would injunct (bar) those decisions by the three-member commission which were neither unanimous nor by majority.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said irrespective of powers vested in the CEC, the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. “If we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,” it said.The statement came after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, strongly argued for an interim direction to the EC to only take decisions by unanimity during pendency of the petition as the amended CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, gave the CEC enormous powers.The PIL has sought scrutiny of the validity of SIR decisions and ”alterations” in Form 6 for new voters. Singh said since the court could not undo elections, a direction must be issued that in the interregnum, EC must follow the statutory mandate. He pleaded that EC be directed to preserve all records on SIR decisions and Form 6 alteration and produce them before SC for scrutiny.Let us have some authenticated facts before us through their responses.They must respond in a clear and transparent manner. If the records show some of the decisions are not taken by majority, we will injunct those. But we cannot put the cart before the horse, the bench said while also issuing notices to the Centre, deputy EC Manish Garg and EC’s director general (IT) Seema Khanna.This has set the stage for the CEC and, more crucially, the two ECs to either endorse or rebut the allegation that important decisions on SIR were taken by Gyanesh Kumar unilaterally and in violation of the law which lays down that the commission’s calls are to be made either unanimously or, failing that, by majority. The allegation, based on a newspaper report, is at the core of the controversy which has reignited opposition to SIR.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, also questioned the validity of Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provided that “no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is, or was, a CEC or an election commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function”.He said this was way beyond the immunity enjoyed even by SC judges and especially when it was not extended even to the PM.Justice Bagchi said, “We will examine the expression ‘or was’. Protection while in office is understandable. Such protection (as provided under Section 16) is perhaps only with regard to the President. It is not given to constitutional court judges under Judges Inquiry Act.”Singh pleaded for suspension of the CEC or divesting him of his authority. When the bench asked who would conduct elections, Singh said the other two ECs would do it. He said in the interim, the SC-mandated selection panel for CEC should be brought back in which the CJI is included along with the PM and the LoP. The 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union minister nominated by the PM.When the bench declined, Singh said the situation was so grave that it could undermine the very basis of our democracy. “Today, the CEC is acting in a manner which is contrary to the statute under which he is appointed. Court should pass some interim orders (restraining the CEC from discharging his functions), otherwise the country will burn,” he said.Patna-based petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh has sought a direction to EC to “produce before SC the complete original and primary records relating to the matters pleaded herein, including minutes, agendas, approvals, file notings, work allocation and delegation orders, IT-access records, server logs, audit trails and database-change histories concerning the functioning of the commission, ERONet/EClNet, alteration of Form 6 and filing of appeals before the Bengal appellate tribunals”.
Article Summary: ‘decisions must be unanimous or by majority’, says supreme court. Cec, ecs need to either rebut or endorse allegations about ‘unilateral decisions’ ‘if we come across instances (where cec has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,’ it said.

Article Title: Cabinet okays new body to bring roads, rail, ports, aviation under one planning framework
Article Text:
The agency will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more (ANI Photo).

NEW DELHI: The Cabinet on Tuesday approved setting up India’s first integrated transport and logistics authority, giving the new body a mandate to plan, appraise and monitor projects worth over Rs 500 crore across roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways, urban mobility and logistics.The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) is aimed at ending fragmented planning across multiple transport ministries and agencies and driving greater coordination and multi-modal integration in infrastructure development. Announcing the decision, I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, “By fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration, ITLA is a new institution responsible for prospective planning for infrastructure development in the country. ”The new agency is modelled on similar institutions in the US, UK, Germany, Australia and Japan, and was first reported by TOI in April 2024.Govt said ITLA will also create a unified transport data repository by obtaining relevant transport and logistics datasets from multiple sources, including GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS-based systems, urban traffic management systems and other databases. It will undertake data analytics for planning, monitoring and impact assessment.Each transport and logistics-related ministry will have an ITLA division to ensure better coordination and implementation of projects and schemes, officials said.The agency will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more. It will also evaluate five-year sectoral plans and annual plans of transport ministries to ensure consistency with the master plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.Vaishnaw said ITLA will coordinate the resolution of inter-ministerial issues and assess the impact of projects after their completion, making post-completion assessment an important part of its mandate.
Article Summary: The integrated transport and logistics authority (itla) is aimed at ending fragmented planning across multiple transport ministries and agencies. The agency will prepare a comprehensive national transport master plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more.

NEW DELHI: Opposition parties on Wednesday sought an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu to raise issues related to chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, sources told news agency ANI.The move came a day after INDIA bloc leaders held a protest against the Election Commission and the CEC over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Meanwhile, Congress chief and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge has invited opposition MPs for lunch at 1pm in Delhi.During the meeting, the MPs are expected to sign a letter seeking an appointment with CEC Gyanesh Kumar, as news agency ANI quoted sources.The INDIA bloc has been demanding answers from the Election Commission on SIR and has accused the poll panel of not addressing its concerns. The protest was part of the opposition's wider “Save Democracy” campaign.On Tuesday, leaders of several INDIA bloc parties marched towards Nirvachan Sadan but were stopped by barricades.The leaders then staged a sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan. During the protest, Rahul Gandhi claimed that around 300 Opposition MPs wanted to meet the election commissioners and submit their concerns.Several opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, were later detained by Delhi Police.Rahul Gandhi defended the protest, saying the opposition only wanted to meet the election commissioners and raise questions about the revision of electoral rolls.After the protest, the Election Commission said no political party had sought an appointment with the poll panel until 4pm.In a statement, the EC said Delhi Police informed it around 4pm that a delegation of around 240 MPs, led by Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, wanted to meet the election commissioners and submit a memorandum at the Parliament House Annexe.The poll panel said the proposed venue and the way the meeting was sought were “unusual” given its established protocol.The Election Commission said it later considered sending its most senior executive officer to receive the memorandum from the opposition MPs at the venue. However, the offer was rejected.
